pr_title: Use a provider to load public keys read from DER encoded data
pr_body:
When reading a SubjectPublicKeyInfo structure (as might be found in an X509 certificate as well as a number of other structures) we should use a provider (via a decoder) unless there is an ENGINE for the public key present.

Fixing this problem was relatively straight forward, but doing so revealed a long list of other problems that this change revealed. Most of the commits in this PR are fixing other issues in order to get the tests to pass following the above change.

Fixes #15393 
Fixes #15327

issue_context.title: x509_pubkey_decode() does not consider algorithms provided by providers.
issue_context.body:
`x509_pubkey_ex_d2i)()` calls x509_pubkey_decode() but it is legacy (even says so in the comments...se below) so if the algorithm is not associated with a NID, it fails. Of course, this can happen if the algorithm is provided via a provider. 

```
/*
 * Attempt to decode a public key.
 * Returns 1 on success, 0 for a decode failure and -1 for a fatal
 * error e.g. malloc failure.
 *
 * This function is #legacy.
 */
static int x509_pubkey_decode(EVP_PKEY **ppkey, const X509_PUBKEY *key)

```
comments:
> so if the algorithm is not associated with a NID, it fails. Of course, this can happen if the algorithm is provided via a provider.

Yes?  This is by design, and is reflected in this code:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/cc9f9b98997ce3aca276dc6dbbe6d98efab4e65d/crypto/x509/x_pubkey.c#L137-L168

In other words, we *try* to use it first, and if that fails (non-fatally), we then try with provider friendly code.

It seems we missed something, though.  This is currently investigated...
I'm working on fixes in this area...watch this space...
@mattcaswell  : Thanks for letting me know.  I'll keep my eyes peeled!  :+1:

review_comments: Yes. This function only does legacy loading, so unless we're forcing legacy loading we only want to continue if we have an ENGINE for this key type.
